subject: Creativity
title: The Torrance Tests: Measuring Creative Potential
description: One-minute skill: The Torrance Tests: Measuring Creative Potential.

hook.text: IQ tests measure intelligence. The Torrance Tests — created in 1966 — attempt to measure creativity.

buildup.text: E. Paul Torrance asked children to draw unusual pictures and imagine creative uses for everyday objects.

discovery.text: The tests score fluency (how many ideas), originality (how unique), and elaboration (how detailed).

twist.text: Torrance scores predict creative achievement better than IQ does — a 50-year longitudinal study confirmed this.

climax.text: The tests revealed something alarming: American children's creativity scores have declined since 1990.

punchline.text: We measure intelligence obsessively. We barely measure creativity.

quiz.question: What did a 50-year study find about Torrance creativity scores?
options: They predict creative achievement better than IQ

details.summary: The Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking, developed in the 1960s, remain the most widely used creativity assessment. They measure fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration through tasks like alternative uses and incomplete figures. Their predictive validity for creative achievement has...
details.whyItMatters: Torrance Tests provided the first reliable measurement of creative thinking ability. They showed that creativity can be assessed separately from intelligence and predicted real-world creative achievement better than IQ tests.
takeaways: Torrance Tests measure fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration
They predict real-world creative achievement better than IQ scores
The tests are used in education, employment, and research worldwide

faq.question: What do the Torrance Tests measure?
faq.answer: Fluency measures how many ideas you generate. Flexibility measures how many different categories of ideas you produce. Originality measures how unusual your ideas are compared to others. Elaboration measures how much detail you add to your ideas.

faq.question: Are the Torrance Tests reliable?
faq.answer: Longitudinal studies show that Torrance Test scores in childhood predict creative achievement in adulthood more accurately than IQ scores, GPA, or teacher evaluations. The predictive validity has been confirmed over 50-year follow-up studies.
